L23·N5963unmasked layer
This is a weakly selective, polysemantic neuron that peaks mid-sentence on the head word of a fixed collocation right before its complement — e.g. "just" (before a quantity), "amount" (of), "comes" (to), "the" (most common) — rather than on any coherent semantic category; it is strongly suppressed on "as" in "such as", commas, and past-tense verbs like "made".

L26·N6757unmasked layer
This neuron fires on individual digit (or parenthesized sub-clause) tokens inside numeric strings such as clock times and legal/code citations — peaking at the closing element of the number (e.g. the final digit of "5:44 PM", the "(g)" or "(4)" subsection marker) — while being strongly suppressed by digits in the middle of such numeric sequences.

L27·N5558unmasked layer
This neuron is essentially a negative-firing "the" detector: its huge suppressive activations land on the definite article **the** inside fixed idiomatic phrases ("a thing of *the* past", "pat on *the* back", "to say *the* least", "more than meets *the* eye"), while its tiny positive activations are diffuse and occur on ordinary non-"the" words in the same slot (a, following, to, In).

L28·N4605unmasked layer
Fires on the token immediately before a numeral — usually the space (or the leading digit "1") preceding a quantity such as a percentage, large count, clock time, or dimension — i.e. it's a positional "a number starts here" detector rather than a semantic one (it goes strongly negative on the same space slot before other numbers like "24/7", ages, "69th").

Weak positive firing on ordinary mid-sentence continuation tokens (function words like "you"/"to", or first sub-word of a proper name) inside flowing boilerplate prose, while the neuron's real signal is strong negative activation on tokens embedded in structured, enumerated data — digit/measurement lists, email-address characters, comma-separated name+instrument listings, and the "Save As" UI phrase.
